newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: MEDIENOS PLAUSHAS 1996 PROFIT 2.1 MLN LITAS.
newsitem.headline: MEDIENOS PLAUSHAS 1996 PROFIT 2.1 MLN LITAS.

text.p: Lithuanian cardboard and packaging producer Medienos Plaushas said on Friday its net profit fell to 2.1 million litas in 1996 from 5.95 million a year earlier according to internationally audited figures.
Unaudited figures published earlier showed the company's 1996 profit was 2.6 million litas.

Medienos Plaushas managing director Petras Chesna told Reuters by telephone that the profit was 500,000 litas lower because of the cost of the audit conducted by Arthur Andersen and some accounting differences.
"The Arthur Andersen audit decreased our net profit by around 500,000 litas," Chesna said.
The company repeated an earlier forecast that it expected to post a net profit of four million litas in 1997.
At the company shareholders meeting a dividend equal to two percent of the face value of shares as of April 7, 1997 was approved.
The company's share capital totals 20.1 million litas.

"Around 400,000 litas will be paid in dividends," Chesna said. The company has said it would use 22 million litas from increased share capital, profit and loans for investments in the production facilities.
Around 16 percent of Medienos Plaushas is foreign owned, of which 6.7 percent is by Estonia's Hansapak and 5.9 percent by Swiss Pictet & Cie, Chesna said.
